name: World Development Indicators

measures.definition: How expensive everyday consumption is compared with the United States (= 100): purchasing-power parity over the market exchange rate.
Intentional homicides per 100,000 people a year (UNODC figures).
Years a newborn would live at today's death rates.
What people pay for health care themselves each year, per person, in current US dollars: out-of-pocket spending, not insurance premiums (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database).
Practising physicians per 1,000 people, generalists and specialists (WHO Global Health Workforce Statistics).
Unemployed people as a share of the labour force, ILO modelled estimate.
Share of people aged 25 and over who completed at least short-cycle tertiary education (SE.TER.CUAT.ST.ZS, UNESCO Institute for Statistics), for the whole country.
